title: routing: admission control using capacity signals (gate best-effort first)
author: Elena Popov
description:
Summary: Integrates fleet/runtime capacity signals into the routing service to drive tier-aware admission control. Under pressure, we preserve enterprise route budgets by gating best-effort traffic first (throttle/queue/deny depending on configured policy). This is the core routing-side change for Hot-route capacity protection (ENG-4924).

Context: We’ve seen fleet-wide tail latency cascades when one or two high-traffic routes (often best-effort/self-serve) push shared pools into high queue depth, causing p99 latency and 5xx across unrelated enterprise workloads. The gateway limiter (ENG-4922) helps, but we need routing to react to real-time capacity and make tier-aware decisions consistently across regions/pools.

What’s in this PR:
- New capacity signal client in routing (fleet-signal service + runtime aggregate metrics): pulls a low-cardinality “pool pressure” snapshot per (region, model-family, pool) and caches it (default TTL 250ms, bounded jitter).
- Admission control policy evaluation in routing request path:
  - Computes an AdmissionDecision = {allow, allow_degraded, queue, deny} with tier attribution (enterprise vs best-effort) and route_group attribution.
  - Applies “gate best-effort first” rules when pool pressure crosses thresholds: best-effort is denied/queued before enterprise is impacted.
  - Enterprise behavior is budget-based: enterprise requests are admitted until an explicit per-route_group budget is exhausted (budget source is policy engine route budgets; this PR only consumes policy output).
- Deterministic decision logging (structured, sampled): emits a stable decision record including inputs (pressure level, tier, route_group, model-family) and the policy version hash. Intended for auditability during enterprise escalations.
- Backpressure integration: when AdmissionDecision=queue, routing returns a retryable response to gateway with explicit backoff hints (no new customer-facing schema changes in this PR; gateway controls final 429 semantics).
- Feature flags + rollout guardrails:
  - routing.admission_control.enabled (default off)
  - routing.admission_control.allowlist_accounts (empty)
  - routing.admission_control.regions (empty)
  - Safe fallback: if signals are stale/unavailable, routing uses “no-signal” mode (allows traffic) but emits a metric for signal gaps.
- Metrics (low cardinality):
  - routing_admission_decisions_total{decision,tier,route_group,region}
  - routing_capacity_snapshot_age_ms{region,pool}
  - routing_capacity_signal_errors_total{region,source}
  - routing_best_effort_denied_ratio{route_group,region}

Not in scope / follow-ups:
- Gateway 429 reason codes & headers live in ENG-4922 / pr-27441.
- Runtime metrics export lives in ENG-4925 / pr-27435.
- Policy schema changes for budgets/priority classes live in ENG-4923 / pr-27418.
- Global fairness changes (scheduler rewrite) explicitly out of scope.

Implementation notes:
- Signal sources: primary is fleet-signal aggregator (preferred), secondary fallback is runtime aggregate endpoint when aggregator is degraded.
- Pressure model: we treat pressure as a normalized scalar [0..1] computed by fleet-signal service; routing uses configured cutoffs:
  - pressure >= 0.75 => start gating best-effort (queue then deny)
  - pressure >= 0.90 => deny best-effort immediately; enterprise remains allow until budget exhaustion
  - pressure >= 0.97 => allow_degraded for enterprise only if policy permits (routing returns ‘degraded’ marker to downstream; no automatic model fallback in this PR)
- Performance: policy evaluation + signal lookup is designed to add <200µs p50 overhead on routing nodes. Signal cache is in-memory, lock-free read path.

Testing:
- Unit tests: pressure threshold behavior, stale signal handling, decision determinism, allowlist/flag behavior.
- Integration tests (local): routing <-> fleet-signal mock; verifies decision metrics and logs.
- Load test (staging): burst traffic on /v1/chat/completions with best-effort accounts; confirmed enterprise latency preserved while best-effort gets queued/denied.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge with flags off.
2) Enable in us-east for allowlisted enterprise accounts + synthetic best-effort load (game day).
3) Expand allowlist, then regions, then remove allowlist once SRE signs off on dashboards/alerts.

Risk assessment:
- Main risk is incorrect gating due to bad signals or unexpected staleness. Mitigations: TTL bounds, signal-gap metrics, and safe allow fallback when signals are missing (no hard deny without a current snapshot).

Links:
- Linear: ENG-4924
- Related PRs: pr-27435 (runtime metrics), pr-27418 (policy budgets), pr-27411 (gateway tier limiter)
- Incident reference: 2025-11-03 Sev1 fleetwide latency cascade (postmortem linked in Confluence)

Screenshots / dashboards: None included here (dashboards are in observability-pack PR).

conversation: Mina Haddad (review): The overall flow looks right. Two questions: (1) how do we ensure we never deny enterprise due to missing signals, and (2) can we avoid tagging metrics by model id (cardinality)?

Elena Popov (author): (1) In no-signal mode we force decision=allow and emit routing_capacity_signal_errors_total; deny paths require a fresh snapshot. (2) Metrics here use model-family + pool only; no model id tag. I’ll add an explicit assertion in the metric helper to prevent model ids.

Peter Holtz (review): For queue vs deny: returning a retryable response to gateway is fine, but please ensure we don’t accidentally “queue” for streaming requests forever. Can we cap queue duration / add a max retry hint?

Elena Popov (author): Good call. Added max_backoff_ms=2000 and a header for gateway to translate into Retry-After / jitter. Also added test for streaming routes to default to deny when pressure>=0.90 (avoids indefinite queueing).

Vanessa Ortiz (review): On the signal client: please add circuit breaker when fleet-signal service starts timing out so routing doesn’t amplify overload. Also please use bounded jitter on refresh to avoid herd behavior.
Elena Popov (author): Implemented per-region circuit breaker (opens after 10 consecutive timeouts; half-open after 5s) and added +/-50ms jitter to refresh scheduling.
Logan Wright (review): Decision logging: ensure the policy hash and route_group are included, but avoid customer_id in logs by default. If needed, sample + restricted path only.

Elena Popov (author): Updated logger to omit customer_id and request_id by default. Added optional debug logging behind routing.admission_control.debug_logging (off) and documented it as restricted/on-call use only.
Mina Haddad (approval): Looks good. Please follow up with SRE to confirm dashboard panels match the new metric names; otherwise OK to merge.
Robert King (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping cache read path lock-free; perf looks fine.
